cases.final_diagnosis: CNC-02 has a developing mechanical vibration problem: the 4.50 mm/s alarm fired twice (tick 914 at 4.58 mm/s and tick 919 at 4.51 mm/s, E3) and vibration stayed elevated across the 910-929 window (bucket means 4.34 and 4.42 mm/s, E4/E9; raw readings 4.16-4.58 mm/s, E13). Load (E5), temperature (E6), and power (E12) are steady, and comparable machine CNC-04 runs far quieter (E11), so this is not an operating change, thermal effect, or sensor glitch - it points to spindle-bearing wear, imbalance, alignment, or loose mounting. The exact mechanical cause is not yet pinpointed. Confidence 0.85, below the 0.90 threshold for a parts replacement. A maintenance inspection (bearing play, mounting, alignment, balance) or continued readings above 4.50 mm/s with a rising trend would raise confidence and justify replace_bearing.

The inspection failures follow a clear batch-2 alternating pattern: odd-numbered batch-2 jobs failed (job 11 at tick 1086, job 13 at 1222, job 15 at 1364) while even-numbered batch-2 jobs passed (job 12 at 1156, job 14 at 1294, job 16 at 1433) [E3, E4, E10, E12]. Job 10 (batch 1) passed [E4], and the most recent job, 16, passed at tick 1433 [E12], so this is not a steadily worsening fault. Every job routes through all six CNC machines (CNC-01..CNC-06) [E5, E6, E7, E9, E10], so no single station is implicated (H2 contradicted), and the failures are specific odd jobs rather than random noise (H3 contradicted). We only have current speed settings (E8) with no history of changes; since all jobs use the same machines, static per-machine speeds cannot explain odd/even alternation, and there is no evidence settings changed over time (H4 unsupported). Q10: the only job after 15 with an inspection result is job 16, which passed at tick 1433 (batch 2) [E12]; E13 returns empty for 1435-1500 as expected. Q11: settings history is unavailable, but the parity pattern cannot be produced by per-machine speeds common to all jobs. Confidence: 0.85. Evidence that would raise it: a vibration trend showing no abnormal vibration (ruling out a mechanical/H4 cause), a settings change history, or continuation of the alternation on jobs 17/18.

Inspection failures are confined to jobs 1, 2 and 4 of batch 1; job 3 passed. All four jobs ran the identical route (CNC-01 → CNC-02 → CNC-03 → CNC-04 → CNC-05) before inspection, so a persistent machine fault or a setting change cannot explain why job 3 passed while its neighbors failed (E3, E4, E6, E10, E11). Maintenance records show recent spindle-noise, coolant and sensor checks all in range (E7), and vibration trends for CNC-01 and CNC-02 show no rising fault signature (E12, E13). The best-supported explanation is material variation within batch 1 (H2) or inspection randomness (H4); an intermittent equipment fault (H3) remains possible but is not evidenced. No hypothesis reaches the 0.90 confidence needed to approve a repair, and none of the available actions (bearing, setting reset, servo drive, hydraulics) would fix a material cause.

CNC-01 had a transient vibration spike: readings were ~2.0–2.5 mm/s baseline through tick 520, jumped to 7.01–7.37 mm/s (above the 4.50 mm/s alarm setpoint) at ticks 521–524, then returned to ~2.2–2.4 mm/s at tick 525 and stayed there through tick 530. During the spike, machine load was unchanged (~66–69%, E6/E8), speed remained at 1000 rpm (E9), and no job change occurred around tick 521 (E7). Alarms fired only at ticks 521–524 (E5). This is a transient disturbance or momentary sensor interference, not a sustained shift, operating change, or developing equipment failure; the machine is back to normal operation.

CNC-03's vibration reading spiked above the 4.50 mm/s threshold for ticks 71-78 (5.00-5.21 mm/s, per E4 and E10) while the machine showed no corresponding operating abnormality: load stayed near zero throughout (E5), temperature stayed normal around 68-74°F (E6), and power stayed steady around 1.6-2.35 kW (E12). The vibration then collapsed to 0.37 mm/s at tick 79 and 0.17 mm/s at tick 80 (E10), with no further alarms (E4 ends at tick 78) and a near-zero minimum inside the alarm window (E13). A neighboring machine, CNC-01, shows normal vibration (E9), so this is not a factory-wide sensor problem. The pattern - sustained spurious high readings that vanish abruptly with no load, temperature, or power signature - indicates a malfunctioning or disturbed vibration sensor on CNC-03, not a genuine mechanical fault. The alarm has already self-cleared. Confidence 0.82; below the 0.90 threshold required for an intervene, and none of the human-approvable actions (bearing, servo drive, hydraulics, reset setting) addresses a sensor, so no mechanical change is warranted.
